newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merger hopes in Nordic insurance boost Finnish shares.
newsitem.headline: Merger hopes in Nordic insurance boost Finnish shares.

text.p: Finnish shares ended higher on Monday as the financial sector was buoyed by hopes of more restructuring in Nordic finance after reports that Swedish insurer Skandia and mortgage bank Stadshypotek may merge.
The HEX general index rose 0.26 percent to close at 2,408.42 and advancing issues beat decliners by 53 to 24. Volume was a brisk 457 million markka.
The Swedish merger plan sparked speculation of major
restructuring in the Nordic financial sector. In Finland, there was speculation that insurance major Pohjola would merge with Sweden's Skandia.
Pohjola closed lively trade up 0.60 markka at 104.50.
Finland's largest bank Merita which owns 16 percent of Pohjola was propelled to a new 14.90 markka 17-month high but ended slightly off its peak at 14.70, still up 0.30.

Investors remained bullish on telecommunications group Nokia after the company's third quarter interim report almost two weeks ago. The share closed up two markka at 265.00 after touching a new 268 markka year-high.
